chapters.title: Talk, talk, talk
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: validation talk as false progress. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Replace announcement with protected private labor until the work has earned the right to be seen.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating silence as secrecy or timidness instead of as a way to keep reward attached to actual work.

chapters.title: To be or to do?
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: status identity versus contribution. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Choose the task that deepens contribution when status and useful work begin pulling in different directions.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the choice into anti-career posturing instead of a live test of loyalty when incentives split.

chapters.title: Become a student
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: apprenticeship over self-certainty. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Move from proving you are already formed to arranging yourself where correction can still reach you.
chapters.commonMisread: Making studenthood sound like passive humility rather than active exposure to feedback and standards.

chapters.title: Don't be passionate
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: discipline over ego-heavy intensity. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Separate durable commitment from the dramatic feeling of being all-in.
chapters.commonMisread: Reading the warning as anti-care, when the target is performative heat that cannot survive repetition.

chapters.title: Follow the canvas strategy
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: indirect leverage through service. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Create leverage by making other people and the larger work more effective before asking to be central.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing service to being nice or invisible instead of deliberately building the conditions where the work can move.

chapters.title: Restrain yourself
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: control over egoic self-expression. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Hold back the satisfying display until timing, role, and consequences justify expression.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating restraint as silence at all costs instead of disciplined timing under provocation.

chapters.title: Get out of your own head
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: ego's inward loop of self-absorption. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Shift attention from self-monitoring to the next external evidence the work needs.
chapters.commonMisread: Making it a cheerful confidence lesson rather than a hard exit from both self-praise and self-loathing.

chapters.title: The danger of early pride
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: premature identity inflation before development is stable. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Keep early signals provisional so they do not harden into an identity that refuses development.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing earned confidence with premature pride, or treating every good sign as dangerous.

chapters.title: Work, work, work
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: labor, patience, and invisible repetition as the answer to ego. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Return every impressive self-story to the next unglamorous repetition the craft requires.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning labor into hustle theater instead of quiet repetition that produces evidence.

chapters.title: For everything that comes next, ego is the enemy...
chapters.sourcePressure: Aspire section: Aspire-stage interstitial handoff into success. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Carry the anti-ego discipline across the threshold instead of assuming progress has purified you.
chapters.commonMisread: Padding the interstitial into a full new system rather than preserving it as a compact warning.

chapters.title: Always stay a student
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: continued teachability as the first defense against success-stage ego. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: After recognition arrives, deliberately re-enter rooms where your assumptions can be corrected.
chapters.commonMisread: Repeating chapter 3 without the success pressure: the danger now is feeling certified by achievement.

chapters.title: Don't tell yourself a story
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: resisting self-narration as a success-stage ego distortion. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Interrupt the flattering narrative before it edits facts into proof of specialness.
chapters.commonMisread: Making it about storytelling skill rather than the private myth that protects ego from evidence.

chapters.title: What's important to you?
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: value clarity as a defense against success-stage priority drift. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Rank what matters before success offers shinier substitutes for importance.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the question into vague life purpose instead of a practical sorting test under pressure.

chapters.title: Entitlement, control, and paranoia
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: linked defensive distortions that success can produce under ego. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Spot the moment ownership of success becomes entitlement, overcontrol, or suspicion.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the three words as separate flaws instead of one defensive cluster around threatened ego.

chapters.title: Managing yourself
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: inward governance as the answer to defensive success. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Turn the management problem inward before trying to tighten control over everyone else.
chapters.commonMisread: Making self-management into routine optimization instead of governance of reactions under success pressure.

chapters.title: Beware the disease of me
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: self-centrality as a success-stage corruption of proportion. Supported by frozen source sidecar.
chapters.coreMove: Notice when every event is being interpreted as a referendum on you, then restore proportion.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing it to narcissism labeling rather than catching the everyday drift toward self-reference.

chapters.title: Meditate on the immensity
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: scale, history, and perspective against self-importance. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Use scale deliberately to shrink the self back to its proper size before making the next decision.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning scale into poetic awe instead of a practical correction to inflated importance.

chapters.title: Maintain your sobriety
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: keeping success from becoming intoxication. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Treat applause, money, and access as intoxicants that require clear rules before judgment changes.
chapters.commonMisread: Making sobriety only literal, or reducing it to asceticism instead of clear judgment around success rewards.

chapters.title: For what often comes next, ego is the enemy...
chapters.sourcePressure: Success section: Success-stage interstitial pivot toward failure. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Prepare for the fall while things still look strong, so failure does not get to define the next posture.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating it as ominous filler rather than a precise bridge from distortion in success to distortion in failure.

chapters.title: Alive time or dead time?
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: active use of setback versus passive suffering. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Convert waiting, loss, or constraint into usable work before resentment converts it into dead time.
chapters.commonMisread: Making every setback positive instead of distinguishing active use from passive decay.

chapters.title: The effort is enough
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: detaching worth from applause and returning it to disciplined effort. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Place the standard inside the effort you control when outcomes refuse to reward you.
chapters.commonMisread: Using effort as an excuse for weak standards rather than as the only honest score when results are unfair.

chapters.title: Fight club moments
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: humiliation and forced correction as a reality test. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Use the hit to locate the weak point before ego turns pain into performance or denial.
chapters.commonMisread: Glamorizing humiliation or conflict instead of treating the painful moment as evidence.

chapters.title: Draw the line
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: boundaries against self-betrayal, resentment, and egoic overreaction. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Choose the boundary that protects character when failure tempts you to explain, retaliate, or bargain.
chapters.commonMisread: Making it about arbitrary toughness instead of a clear moral line under pressure.

chapters.title: Maintain your own scorecard
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: self-honest standards replacing external validation. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Measure against the standard you can defend when public scores misread the work.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the scorecard into private self-flattery rather than a stricter standard than applause or blame.

chapters.title: Always love
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: refusing bitterness after defeat. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: Keep regard for people and reality intact when ego wants failure to become grievance.
chapters.commonMisread: Softening into sentimental forgiveness instead of disciplined refusal to let failure poison the self.

chapters.title: For everything that comes next, ego is the enemy...
chapters.sourcePressure: Failure section: closing the recurring cycle of ego across aspiration, success, and failure. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapters.coreMove: End each cycle by resetting vigilance, because ego returns with the next aspiration, win, or loss.
chapters.commonMisread: Writing a grand inspirational finale instead of a clean return to the repeated discipline.
